name: Verish' Ne Verish'
description: Verish' Ne Verish' ('Believe It or Not') is the Russian version of BS/Cheat. 2-6+ players. Deal all cards. Play face-down declaring rank. Players call 'Ne Veryu!' to challenge. Wrong challengee picks up pile; wrong challenger picks up pile. Shed all cards to win.

history.origins: Verish' Ne Verish' is the Russian equivalent of I Doubt It (Cheat/BS). The name means 'Trust - don't trust'. It belongs to the worldwide family of shedding games where players play face-down, declare ranks, and may be challenged. The game is played in Russia as a family and casual game.
timeline: 20th century: Russian family game; part of the worldwide Cheat/BS shedding family.
history.evolution: Russian version of the worldwide Cheat/BS family.

rules.objective: Get rid of all your cards. Last player left with cards loses.
rules.gameplay: Play 1+ cards face-down declaring rank. Next player: add same rank OR challenge ('Ne Veryu!'). Caught bluffing = pick up pile. Wrong challenge = challenger picks up. Four-of-a-kind auto-discards (variant).
keyRules: Bluffer or challenger picks up pile

strategy.advanced: Bluff when opponents have few cards.

variations.name: I trust and expose
variations.description: Player may say I trust and expose previous play; if lied they pick up, if truth cards go to discard and they start next round. Often no four-of-a-kind discard.
variations.emptyOverridesReason: Variant affects trust/expose flow only; no engine constant overrides documented.

variations.name: No fours discard
variations.description: Players may not discard sets of four equal cards; legal to start a round by playing four cards.
variations.emptyOverridesReason: Variant disables four-of-a-kind discard; add overrides when implementing optional discard rule.

variations.name: Last card wait
variations.description: When a player plays their last cards they must wait until turn comes again and then trust or not trust; if wrong they pick up and stay in the game.
variations.emptyOverridesReason: Variant adds wait-before-win rule; engine overrides to be added when implementing.
